#!/bin/sh
# systemd-shutdown hook (runs last, root read-only, journald gone). If any HDMI
# owner module is still loaded, teardown failed somewhere and holds were
# retained (MIPS unparked, SCP payload possibly still asserting HPD). Those
# need a physical cold cycle, which a warm reset cannot give, so a reboot or
# kexec is turned into a poweroff, lamp off first. Poweroff/halt proceed as
# requested. Never touches hardware itself.
M=${H713_GUARD_SYSMODULE:-/sys/module}
OFF=${H713_GUARD_LAMP_OFF:-/usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/h713-off}
POWEROFF=${H713_GUARD_POWEROFF:-systemctl --force --force poweroff}
held=
for m in h713_hdmi_signal h713_ddc_pins h713_scp_probe h713_hdmi_audio h713_hdmi_receiver; do
  [ ! -d "$M/$m" ] || held="$held $m"
done
[ -n "$held" ] || exit 0
case "$1" in
reboot|kexec)
  msg="h713-hdmi-hold-guard: $1 refused, HDMI holds retained ($held ); powering off, cold cycle required"
  echo "$msg" > /dev/kmsg 2>/dev/null; echo "$msg" > /dev/console 2>/dev/null
  "$OFF" poweroff
  exec $POWEROFF;;
*)
  msg="h713-hdmi-hold-guard: $1 with HDMI holds retained ($held ); cold cycle required"
  echo "$msg" > /dev/kmsg 2>/dev/null; echo "$msg" > /dev/console 2>/dev/null;;
esac
exit 0

#!/bin/sh
# Run on target from the complete build-startup.py bundle. Installs but does
# not start capture or change U-Boot environment. Safe under the bench service.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]
[ "$(uname -r)" = 6.18.38 ]
grep -q 'HY200 QZ713DF_A1' /proc/device-tree/model
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
for module in h713-hdmi-receiver.ko h713-hdmi-audio.ko h713-hdmi-signal.ko h713-ddc-pins.ko; do
  set -- $(modinfo -F vermagic "$module")
  [ "$1" = 6.18.38 ]
done
# Do not replace an installed generation while its service owns hardware.
[ ! -e /usr/lib/h713-hdmi ] || { echo 'Existing startup installation; refusing replacement' >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p /mnt/boot
mountpoint -q /mnt/boot || mount -t vfat /dev/mmcblk0p2 /mnt/boot
[ "$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /mnt/boot)" = /dev/mmcblk0p2 ]
[ "$(stat -c %s /mnt/boot/h713-kernel.fit)" = 7789772 ]
[ ! -e /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr ]
[ ! -e /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-capture.service ]
# The original FIT is untouched. Rollback state is outside the small boot FAT.
install -d -m 0755 /var/lib/h713-hdmi-startup /usr/lib/h713-hdmi
sha256sum /mnt/boot/h713-kernel.fit > /var/lib/h713-hdmi-startup/kernel.sha256
cp -a . /usr/lib/h713-hdmi/
chmod -R go-w /usr/lib/h713-hdmi
install -m 0644 h713-hdmi-capture.service /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-capture.service
install -m 0644 h713-hdmi-signal.service /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-signal.service
install -m 0755 h713-hdmi-hold-guard /usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/h713-hdmi-hold-guard
systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-capture.service /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-signal.service
cp h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr.new
sync
cmp h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr.new
mv /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr.new /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr
sync
cmp h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr
sha256sum -c /var/lib/h713-hdmi-startup/kernel.sha256
# Enable only; the current bench runtime unit must retain ownership this boot.
systemctl enable h713-hdmi-capture.service h713-hdmi-signal.service
echo 'Installed. Activate only after saving the guarded U-Boot environment and a physical cold cycle.'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive the MIPS display firmware's debug shell from the ARM side.

RUNS ON THE BOARD (needs /dev/mem):

    scp tools/mips/mips-shell.py root@192.168.4.1:/root/
    ssh root@192.168.4.1 python3 -u /root/mips-shell.py --status
    ssh root@192.168.4.1 python3 -u /root/mips-shell.py --cmd 'win wi'

WHY THIS EXISTS.  display.bin spawns two shell threads.  `shell_thread_uart`
polls UART4, whose only pin routes are unavailable to us.  `shell_thread_monitor`
runs the *same command parser* over a ring buffer in DRAM, and 2026-08-07
confirmed on hardware that the ring is registered, ARM-reachable and uncached.
It has never been driven.  Doing so gives us the firmware's own `win` command --
`win wi` dumps the live geometry of every WCE window node -- plus `regr`/`regw`,
the MIPS's own view of the fabric.

THE PROTOCOL, recovered from the firmware and confirmed against the live object.
This is SEGGER-RTT-shaped.  A control block at MIPS 0xabd01000:

    +0x00  char acID[16]
    +0x10  MaxNumUpBuffers      (3)
    +0x14  MaxNumDownBuffers    (3)
    +0x18  aUp[3]               24 bytes each -- MIPS writes, we read
    +0x60  aDown[3]             24 bytes each -- we write, MIPS reads

    each descriptor: { sName, pBuffer, SizeOfBuffer, WrOff, RdOff, Flags }

The firmware's own accessors pin the field order beyond doubt: the read path
(`0x8b155af0`, reached from getc `0x8b19d3b4`) loads pBuffer from `+0x64`,
SizeOfBuffer from `+0x68`, WrOff from `+0x6c` and RdOff from `+0x70` -- i.e.
aDown[0] -- and the rx-ready predicate at `0x8b155f78` returns
`WrOff != RdOff` over the same pair.  24-byte stride is explicit in the code as
`(idx*2 + idx) << 3`.

Read live on 2026-09-04 with the MIPS parked, which confirms every field:

    aUp[0]    pBuffer 0xabd01300  size 0x41c00  WrOff 8  RdOff 0
    aDown[0]  pBuffer 0xabd01200  size 0x100    WrOff 0  RdOff 0

and those 8 pending output bytes are `1b 5b 32 4a 1b 5b 31 48` = `ESC[2J
ESC[1H`, the shell clearing its screen during bring-up.  That is firmware
output sitting in the ring, which is as direct a confirmation of the decode as
this project is going to get without running the thing.

ADDRESS WINDOW.  MIPS kseg0/kseg1 map to system addresses through the measured
+0x40000000 window: kseg0 `0x8b232c20` -> `0x4b232c20`, kseg1 `0xabd01000` ->
`0x4bd01000`.

LINE TERMINATOR.  The shell's key table binds both `0x0d` and `0x0a` to the
"enter" handler at `0x8b18337c`, so either works; we send `\\r`.

THE MIPS MUST BE ALIVE, AND GETTING THERE IS THE HARD PART.  Nothing is
consumed while the core is parked -- a staged command simply sits in the ring.
So `--cmd` returning nothing with the core parked is not a failure of this tool.

Releasing the core from a booted Linux **hard-locked the whole SoC** on
2026-09-04: network and serial both dead, physical power cycle.  There was no
video running, so the documented "MIPS + Cedrus traffic" rule did not cover it.
The difference from every earlier, successful release at the U-Boot prompt is
that our KMS driver was bound and owning the display when the window layer came
up.  Hence `--unbind`, and `--release` refusing to run without it.

WHY NOT DO THIS FROM U-BOOT INSTEAD, which is the obvious answer and does not
work: U-Boot maps all DRAM from 0x40000000 as MT_NORMAL cacheable
(`sunxi_mem_map` in arch/arm/mach-sunxi/board.c), D-cache is on
(`CONFIG_SYS_DCACHE_OFF` unset) and `CONFIG_CMD_CACHE` is **not** set, so there
is no `dcache off`.  `md`/`mw` do no cache maintenance, so a command written
with `mw.l` would sit in the ARM's D-cache where the MIPS -- which reads this
memory uncached through kseg1, outside the ARM's coherency domain -- cannot see
it, and polling the up-ring offsets with `md.l` would be answered from a stale
cache line.  U-Boot's own code proves the incoherency: `h713_mips.c` calls
`flush_cache()` after loading the firmware and `invalidate_dcache_range()`
before reading anything the MIPS wrote.  The 2026-08-07 probe that read this
block from the U-Boot prompt only ever did a *cold first read*, which is the one
case that works regardless.  Making the U-Boot route work means adding cache
maintenance to U-Boot and flashing the bootloader, since FEL boot is documented
as non-working on this SoC.

Linux has no such problem: /dev/mem maps the carveout as Device memory, which is
uncached -- proven the hard way by the SIGBUS documented on `Mem` below.

PRIVILEGE CAVEAT, unresolved.  In the shell's command table `win` carries flag
word `0x2000`, the same as `regw`, while `regr`/`cmds`/`keys` carry `0x2100`.
There is a `users` command and a "default user" entry, so `0x2000` may be a
privilege level the monitor stream does not have.  If `win` comes back
rejected, that is the first thing to look at -- try `cmds` first, which is
`0x2100` and should always work.
"""
import argparse
import ctypes
import mmap
import os
import struct
import sys
import time

DEVICE_GLOBAL = 0x4B232C20      # system address of the pointer to the block
PAGE = 0x1000


def mips_to_sys(addr):
    """kseg0/kseg1 MIPS address -> system physical, via the +0x40000000 window."""
    if 0x80000000 <= addr < 0xA0000000:
        return addr - 0x80000000 + 0x40000000
    if 0xA0000000 <= addr < 0xC0000000:
        return addr - 0xA0000000 + 0x40000000
    return addr


class Mem:
    """/dev/mem accessed strictly as aligned 32-bit words.

    THIS IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE. The MIPS carveout (`4b100000-4d960fff` in
    /proc/iomem, reserved) maps through /dev/mem as **Device memory**, which on
    arm64 does not tolerate unaligned or multi-register accesses. Python's
    `mmap` slicing is a memcpy and SIGBUSes on it -- non-deterministically,
    because whether it faults depends on which memcpy path the length selects:
    a 16-byte read of the control block succeeded and a 24-byte read of the
    same address died. `busybox devmem` never had trouble because it issues one
    aligned volatile word load.

    So every access here goes through a ctypes uint32 view, and byte-level
    writes become read-modify-write of the covering words.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.fd = os.open("/dev/mem", os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        self.maps = {}

    def _words(self, base):
        if base not in self.maps:
            page = mmap.mmap(self.fd, PAGE, mmap.MAP_SHARED,
                             mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=base)
            self.maps[base] = (page, (ctypes.c_uint32 * (PAGE // 4)).from_buffer(page))
        return self.maps[base][1]

    def u32(self, addr):
        if addr & 3:
            raise ValueError(f"unaligned 32-bit read at {addr:#x}")
        return self._words(addr & ~(PAGE - 1))[(addr & (PAGE - 1)) // 4]

    def put32(self, addr, value):
        if addr & 3:
            raise ValueError(f"unaligned 32-bit write at {addr:#x}")
        self._words(addr & ~(PAGE - 1))[(addr & (PAGE - 1)) // 4] = value & 0xFFFFFFFF

    def read(self, addr, length):
        """Bytes, assembled from the covering aligned words."""
        first = addr & ~3
        last = (addr + length + 3) & ~3
        raw = b"".join(struct.pack("<I", self.u32(a))
                       for a in range(first, last, 4))
        start = addr - first
        return raw[start:start + length]

    def write(self, addr, data):
        """Bytes, via read-modify-write of the covering aligned words."""
        first = addr & ~3
        last = (addr + len(data) + 3) & ~3
        raw = bytearray(b"".join(struct.pack("<I", self.u32(a))
                                 for a in range(first, last, 4)))
        raw[addr - first:addr - first + len(data)] = data
        for i, a in enumerate(range(first, last, 4)):
            self.put32(a, struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, i * 4)[0])


class Buffer:
    """One RTT-shaped ring descriptor."""

    FIELDS = 24

    def __init__(self, mem, desc_addr):
        self.mem = mem
        self.addr = desc_addr
        name, buf, size, wr, rd, flags = struct.unpack("<6I", mem.read(desc_addr, 24))
        self.name_ptr = name
        self.buffer = mips_to_sys(buf) if buf else 0
        self.size = size
        self.flags = flags

    @property
    def wroff(self):
        return self.mem.u32(self.addr + 12)

    @wroff.setter
    def wroff(self, value):
        self.mem.put32(self.addr + 12, value)

    @property
    def rdoff(self):
        return self.mem.u32(self.addr + 16)

    @rdoff.setter
    def rdoff(self, value):
        self.mem.put32(self.addr + 16, value)

    def __repr__(self):
        return (f"buf={self.buffer:#010x} size={self.size:#x} "
                f"wr={self.wroff} rd={self.rdoff} flags={self.flags:#x}")


class Terminal:
    def __init__(self):
        self.mem = Mem()
        ptr = self.mem.u32(DEVICE_GLOBAL)
        if not ptr:
            sys.exit(f"device global {DEVICE_GLOBAL:#x} is zero -- "
                     "the firmware has never published its debug terminal")
        self.block = mips_to_sys(ptr)
        head = self.mem.read(self.block, 0x18)
        self.acid = head[:16]
        self.n_up, self.n_down = struct.unpack("<2I", head[16:24])
        if not (1 <= self.n_up <= 8 and 1 <= self.n_down <= 8):
            sys.exit(f"control block at {self.block:#x} does not look like one "
                     f"(up={self.n_up} down={self.n_down}) -- refusing to write")
        self.up = [Buffer(self.mem, self.block + 0x18 + i * 24)
                   for i in range(self.n_up)]
        self.down = [Buffer(self.mem, self.block + 0x18 + (self.n_up + i) * 24)
                     for i in range(self.n_down)]

    # -- output: MIPS wrote, we consume -----------------------------------
    def drain(self, index=0):
        buf = self.up[index]
        if not buf.buffer or not buf.size:
            return b""
        wr, rd = buf.wroff, buf.rdoff
        if wr == rd:
            return b""
        if wr > rd:
            data = self.mem.read(buf.buffer + rd, wr - rd)
        else:
            data = (self.mem.read(buf.buffer + rd, buf.size - rd) +
                    self.mem.read(buf.buffer, wr))
        buf.rdoff = wr
        return data

    # -- input: we write, MIPS consumes -----------------------------------
    def send(self, text, index=0):
        buf = self.down[index]
        if not buf.buffer or not buf.size:
            sys.exit(f"down buffer {index} is not configured")
        data = text.encode()
        wr, rd = buf.wroff, buf.rdoff
        # One byte is always left unused so full and empty stay distinguishable
        # -- the firmware's own readers treat WrOff == RdOff as empty.
        free = (rd - wr - 1) % buf.size
        if len(data) > free:
            sys.exit(f"command is {len(data)} bytes and only {free} are free "
                     f"in the {buf.size}-byte down buffer; is the MIPS parked?")
        for byte in data:
            self.mem.write(buf.buffer + wr, bytes([byte]))
            wr = (wr + 1) % buf.size
        # Read the payload back before publishing it. /dev/mem may map this
        # region cached, in which case our bytes could still be in the ARM's
        # cache while the MIPS reads stale DRAM. This does not prove coherency,
        # but a mismatch here proves the absence of it, cheaply.
        start = buf.wroff
        if start + len(data) <= buf.size:
            echo = self.mem.read(buf.buffer + start, len(data))
            if echo != data:
                sys.exit(f"readback mismatch: wrote {data!r}, read {echo!r} -- "
                         "the mapping is probably cached; do not trust this path")
        buf.wroff = wr          # publish last, after the payload is in place
        return len(data)


MIPS_RESET_STATUS = 0x0306101C

# h713_mips_release_reset() from arch/arm/mach-sunxi/h713_mips.c, in order.
# The firmware is already resident and its shared memory published by the
# preboot, so re-releasing a quiesced core needs nothing else.
RELEASE_SEQUENCE = [
    (0x02001600, 0x80000002, "clock"),
    (0x0200160C, 0x00000000, "reset asserted"),
    (0x0200160C, 0x00010000, "stage 1"),
    (0x0200160C, 0x00030000, "stage 2"),
    (0x0200160C, 0x00030001, "stage 3"),
    (0x03061030, 0x4B100000, "boot address"),
    (0x0200160C, 0x00070001, "RELEASED"),
]

DRM_DRIVER = "/sys/bus/platform/drivers/sun50i-h713-afbd"
DRM_DEVICE = "5600000.display"


def kmsg(text):
    """Log to the kernel ring, which reaches the serial console immediately.

    When the SoC locked on 2026-09-04 the ssh session died mid-script and took
    the progress output with it, so we could not tell which write did it. This
    goes out the UART as it happens and survives the lock.
    """
    try:
        with open("/dev/kmsg", "w") as handle:
            handle.write(f"mips-shell: {text}\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


def display_driver_bound():
    return os.path.exists(os.path.join(DRM_DRIVER, DRM_DEVICE))


def unbind_display():
    """Take our KMS driver off the display hardware.

    THE REASON THIS EXISTS.  Releasing the MIPS from a booted Linux hard-locked
    the whole SoC on 2026-09-04 -- network and serial both dead, physical power
    cycle.  There was no video running, so the previously documented
    "MIPS + Cedrus traffic" rule did not cover it.  What was different from
    every earlier (successful) release at the U-Boot prompt is that our KMS
    driver was bound, holding the AFBD/route/LVDS windows and the AFBD IRQ,
    when the window layer came up and took presentation.

    So: remove the second owner first.  This is the hypothesis under test, not
    an established fix -- if the SoC locks again with the driver unbound, then
    two-owner contention was the wrong explanation.
    """
    if not display_driver_bound():
        return "already unbound"
    kmsg("unbinding the KMS driver before releasing the MIPS")
    with open(os.path.join(DRM_DRIVER, "unbind"), "w") as handle:
        handle.write(DRM_DEVICE)
    time.sleep(1.0)
    if display_driver_bound():
        sys.exit("unbind did not take -- refusing to release the core")
    return "unbound"


def release_core(mem):
    """Replay the release sequence, narrating to the UART as we go."""
    kmsg("releasing the MIPS core -- if this is the last line, the SoC locked")
    for addr, value, what in RELEASE_SEQUENCE:
        kmsg(f"  {addr:#010x} <- {value:#010x}  {what}")
        print(f"  {addr:#010x} <- {value:#010x}  {what}", flush=True)
        mem.put32(addr, value)
        time.sleep(0.15)
    time.sleep(2.0)
    status = mem.u32(MIPS_RESET_STATUS)
    kmsg(f"core released, status={status:#x} -- survived the release")
    return status


def mips_alive(mem):
    """1 = the core is running.

    Read through the mmap path, not a plain read() on /dev/mem: this is MMIO
    with no linear mapping, and read() on it SIGBUSes on arm64. That cost a
    debugging round trip -- the mmap of the same address is fine, which is why
    `busybox devmem` had no trouble with it.
    """
    return mem.u32(MIPS_RESET_STATUS) == 1


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--status", action="store_true", help="describe the rings and exit")
    parser.add_argument("--drain", action="store_true", help="print pending output and exit")
    parser.add_argument("--cmd", help="send a command line, then read the reply")
    parser.add_argument("--wait", type=float, default=1.5, help="seconds to wait for output")
    parser.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true", help="hex-dump output instead of decoding")
    parser.add_argument("--unbind", action="store_true",
                        help="take the KMS driver off 5600000.display first")
    parser.add_argument("--release", action="store_true",
                        help="release the MIPS core (refuses while the KMS driver is bound)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    term = Terminal()
    alive = mips_alive(term.mem)

    if args.unbind:
        print(f"[KMS driver: {unbind_display()}]", flush=True)

    if args.release:
        if alive:
            print("[the core is already running -- not releasing it again]", flush=True)
        elif display_driver_bound():
            sys.exit("REFUSING: sun50i-h713-afbd is still bound to 5600000.display.\n"
                     "Releasing the core with a second owner of the display hard-locked\n"
                     "the SoC on 2026-09-04. Pass --unbind, or unbind it yourself.")
        else:
            status = release_core(term.mem)
            alive = status == 1
            print(f"[core status {status:#010x}"
                  f"{'' if alive else '  !! NOT ALIVE'}]", flush=True)

    if args.status or not (args.drain or args.cmd):
        print(f"control block  {term.block:#010x}  acID {term.acid!r}")
        print(f"MIPS core      {'ALIVE' if alive else 'parked'} (0x0306101c)")
        for i, buf in enumerate(term.up):
            print(f"  up[{i}]   {buf}")
        for i, buf in enumerate(term.down):
            print(f"  down[{i}] {buf}")
        if not args.status:
            return
        return

    def show(data, label):
        if not data:
            print(f"[{label}: nothing]")
            return
        if args.raw:
            print(f"[{label}: {len(data)} bytes]")
            print(data.hex(" "))
        else:
            print(f"[{label}: {len(data)} bytes]")
            sys.stdout.write(data.decode("latin1"))
            sys.stdout.flush()
            print()

    if args.drain:
        show(term.drain(), "drained")
        return

    stale = term.drain()
    if stale:
        show(stale, "stale output, discarded before the command")

    n = term.send(args.cmd + "\r")
    print(f"[sent {n} bytes: {args.cmd!r}]")
    if not alive:
        print("[the MIPS is PARKED -- the command is staged in the ring and will")
        print(" be consumed when the core is released; expect no reply now]")

    deadline = time.time() + args.wait
    out = b""
    while time.time() < deadline:
        out += term.drain()
        time.sleep(0.05)
    show(out, "reply")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    0xc002: "return-send-enter", 0xc009: "return-ack-wait",

                        help="bounded watch duration in seconds (maximum 60)")
    parser.add_argument("--interval", type=float, default=0.01,
                        help="poll interval in seconds (0.002..1; default 0.01)")
    parser.add_argument("--kmsg", action="store_true",
                        help="also publish changes to the kernel log/serial console")
    parser.add_argument("--source-only", action="store_true",
                        help="sample only source markers and page guards to reduce poll overhead")

        parser.error("--watch must be between 0 and 60 seconds")

                                 f"{actual:#010x} != {expected:#010x}")

        raise SystemExit(f"unrecognized adapter call patch {adapter_site:#010x}")

    capture_enabled = capture_site == CAPTURE_PATCHED_WORDS[-1][1]
    if capture_enabled:
        for address, expected in CAPTURE_PATCHED_WORDS:
            actual = mem.u32(address)
            if actual != expected:

                                 f"{actual:#010x} != {expected:#010x}")

        raise SystemExit(f"unrecognized VIncap hook {capture_site:#010x}")

        raise SystemExit("comm-trace magic absent; refusing to interpret mailbox")

            mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0xffc) != CANARY):
        raise SystemExit("comm-trace page guard absent; refusing to interpret mailbox")

    def sample():
        guards = (mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x80), mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0xffc))
        adapter = ({
            "adapter": f"{mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x58):04x}",
            "requested": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x5c),
            "callback_object": f"{mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x60):08x}",
            "dispatch_target": f"{mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x64):08x}",
            "dispatch_source": f"{mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x68):08x}",
            "source3_callback_event0": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x6c),
            "source3_worker_event0": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x70),
            "source3_worker_old": f"{mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x74):08x}",
            "source3_worker_new": f"{mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x78):08x}",
            "source3_transition_complete": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x7c),
        } if adapter_enabled else {})
        capture = ({
            "cap_irq": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x84),
            "cap_vde": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x88),
            "cap_vs": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x8c),
            "cap_mode_change": mem.u32(MAILBOX + 0x90),
        } if capture_enabled else {})
        if args.source_only:
            callback, event, new, old, source_queue, worker, vp_init = (
                mem.u32(MAILBOX + off) for off in
                (0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x2c, 0x30, 0x34, 0x38))
            return {
                "guards": f"{guards[0]:08x}/{guards[1]:08x}",
                **adapter, **capture,
                "callback": f"{callback:04x}:{SOURCE_STAGES.get(callback, 'other')}",
                "worker": f"{worker:04x}:{SOURCE_STAGES.get(worker, 'other')}",
                "event": event, "new": new, "old": old,
                "source_queue": f"{source_queue:08x}",
                "vp_init": f"{vp_init:04x}",
            }
        values = [mem.u32(MAILBOX + off) for off in
                  (0x00, 0x08, 0x0c, 0x10, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x2c,
                   0x30, 0x34, 0x38, 0x40, 0x44, 0x48, 0x4c, 0x50, 0x54)]
        (comm, queue, call, ack, callback, event, new, old, source_queue,
         worker, vp_init, frame, dirty, mode, control, commit, dirty_latch) = values
        return {
            "guards": f"{guards[0]:08x}/{guards[1]:08x}",
            **adapter, **capture,
            "comm": f"{comm:04x}:{COMM_STAGES.get(comm, 'other')}",
            "call": f"{call:04x}:{CALL_STAGES.get(call, 'other')}",
            "ack": f"{ack:04x}:{ACK_STAGES.get(ack, 'other')}",
            "queue": f"{queue:08x}",
            "callback": f"{callback:04x}:{SOURCE_STAGES.get(callback, 'other')}",
            "worker": f"{worker:04x}:{SOURCE_STAGES.get(worker, 'other')}",
            "event": event, "new": new, "old": old,
            "source_queue": f"{source_queue:08x}",
            "vp_init": f"{vp_init:04x}", "frame": f"{frame:04x}",
            "dirty": f"{dirty:08x}", "mode": f"{mode:08x}",
            "control": f"{control:08x}", "commit": f"{commit:08x}",
            "dirty_latch": f"{dirty_latch:08x}",
        }

    started = time.monotonic()
    previous = None
    while True:
        now = time.monotonic()
        state = sample()
        state["seconds"] = round(now - started, 3)
        comparable = tuple((key, value) for key, value in state.items()
                           if key != "seconds")
        if comparable != previous or now - started >= args.watch:
            line = json.dumps(state, separators=(",", ":"))
            print(line, flush=True)
            if kmsg:
                kmsg.write("<6>h713-mips-trace: " + line + "\n")
            previous = comparable
        if now - started >= args.watch:
            break
        time.sleep(min(args.interval, args.watch - (now - started)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/bin/sh
# Run on target from a complete build-startup.py bundle. Replaces ONLY the
# signal owner files (signal module, DDC helper, wrapper, the shutdown hold
# guard and its systemd-shutdown copy, the fresh-install script) plus this
# script and SHA256SUMS. Refuses unless every other installed file is
# byte-identical to the bundle, so the U-Boot script, receiver/audio modules, units and firmware
# are never touched. A loaded owner keeps running its in-memory module; the
# new files take effect on the next cold boot. Never stops or starts units.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
I=${H713_HDMI_INSTALL:-/usr/lib/h713-hdmi}
S=${H713_HDMI_STATE:-/var/lib/h713-hdmi-startup}
M=${H713_HDMI_SYSMODULE:-/sys/module}
H=${H713_HDMI_SHUTDOWN_HOOKS:-/usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown}
SCOPE='h713-hdmi-signal.ko h713-ddc-pins.ko h713-hdmi-signal.py h713-hdmi-hold-guard install-startup.sh update-signal-owner.sh'
in_scope() { case " $SCOPE " in *" $1 "*) return 0;; esac; return 1; }
die() { echo "$*; nothing changed" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "${H713_HDMI_INSTALL:-}" ] || [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || die 'run as root'
sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS || die 'bundle checksum mismatch'
[ -d "$I" ] && [ -d "$S" ] && [ -d "$H" ] || die 'no installed startup generation'
# Out-of-scope files must match their own record; scope files may be from an
# interrupted earlier run, which this run simply completes.
(cd "$I" && awk -v scope=" $SCOPE " 'index(scope, " " $2 " ") == 0' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c --quiet) ||
  die 'installed generation fails its own checksums'
# A failed owner is retaining holds for a cold cycle; leave its files alone.
if [ -d "$M/h713_hdmi_signal" ]; then
  [ "$(cat "$M/h713_hdmi_signal/parameters/failed")" = N ] || die 'loaded signal owner has failed'
fi
awk '{print $2}' SHA256SUMS | while read -r f; do
  in_scope "$f" && continue
  [ "$f" = SHA256SUMS ] && continue
  cmp -s "$f" "$I/$f" || { echo "installed $f differs from bundle; refusing signal-owner-only update; nothing changed" >&2; exit 1; }
done
current=1
for f in $SCOPE; do cmp -s "$f" "$I/$f" 2>/dev/null || current=0; done
cmp -s h713-hdmi-hold-guard "$H/h713-hdmi-hold-guard" 2>/dev/null || current=0
if [ $current = 1 ] && cmp -s SHA256SUMS "$I/SHA256SUMS"; then echo 'Signal owner already current'; exit 0; fi
B=$(mktemp -d "$S/signal-owner.$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
for f in $SCOPE SHA256SUMS; do [ ! -e "$I/$f" ] || cp -a "$I/$f" "$B/"; done
[ ! -e "$H/h713-hdmi-hold-guard" ] || cp -a "$H/h713-hdmi-hold-guard" "$B/shutdown-hook.h713-hdmi-hold-guard"
for f in $SCOPE; do
  mode=0644; case $f in *.sh|h713-hdmi-hold-guard) mode=0755;; esac
  [ ! -e "$I/$f" ] || mode=$(stat -c %a "$I/$f")
  install -m $mode "$f" "$I/$f.new"
  sync
  cmp "$f" "$I/$f.new"
  mv "$I/$f.new" "$I/$f"
done
# Executed by systemd-shutdown; a copy, so it never depends on the bundle path.
install -m 0755 h713-hdmi-hold-guard "$H/h713-hdmi-hold-guard.new"
sync
cmp h713-hdmi-hold-guard "$H/h713-hdmi-hold-guard.new"

# Run on target from a complete build-startup.py bundle. Replaces ONLY the
# U-Boot script (FAT h713-hdmi.scr plus the installed .scr/.cmd/SHA256SUMS).
# Refuses unless every other installed file is byte-identical to the bundle,
# so modules, units and firmware owned by running services are never touched.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]
I=/usr/lib/h713-hdmi
S=/var/lib/h713-hdmi-startup
sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS
[ -d "$I" ] && [ -f "$S/kernel.sha256" ]
mountpoint -q /mnt/boot || mount -t vfat /dev/mmcblk0p2 /mnt/boot
[ "$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /mnt/boot)" = /dev/mmcblk0p2 ]
sha256sum -c --quiet "$S/kernel.sha256"
# The FAT script must be the installed generation, not something foreign.
cmp "$I/h713-hdmi.scr" /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr
awk '{print $2}' SHA256SUMS | while read -r f; do
  case "$f" in h713-hdmi.scr|h713-hdmi.cmd|update-startup-script.sh) continue;; esac
  cmp "$f" "$I/$f" || { echo "installed $f differs from bundle; refusing script-only update" >&2; exit 1; }

if cmp -s h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr; then echo 'Startup script already current'; exit 0; fi
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)
cp -a "$I/h713-hdmi.scr" "$S/h713-hdmi.scr.$stamp"
cp -a "$I/h713-hdmi.cmd" "$S/h713-hdmi.cmd.$stamp"
cp h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr.new
sync
cmp h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr.new
mv /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr.new /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr
sync
cmp h713-hdmi.scr /mnt/boot/h713-hdmi.scr
install -m 0644 h713-hdmi.scr h713-hdmi.cmd SHA256SUMS "$I/"
[ -e update-startup-script.sh ] && install -m 0755 update-startup-script.sh "$I/"
(cd "$I" && sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS)

#!/bin/sh
# Read-only check of the automatic HDMI startup path on the target. Prints
# evidence and exits nonzero on the first unmet production condition.
set -u
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; exit 1; }
P=/sys/module
echo "== boot $(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id) $(uname -r) up $(cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/uptime)s"
H=/proc/device-tree/chosen/h713,hdmi-boot-v1
[ -f "$H" ] || fail 'no U-Boot handoff property'
handoff=$(od -An -tx1 -v "$H" | tr -d ' \n'); echo "handoff $handoff"
case "$handoff" in 48444d4900000000????????) ;; *) fail 'handoff not magic/0/pid';; esac
[ "${handoff#48444d4900000000}" != 00000000 ] || fail 'handoff pid zero'
for u in h713-hdmi-capture h713-hdmi-signal; do
  s=$(systemctl show -p ActiveState,Result,ConditionResult,ExecMainStatus --value $u | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "$u: $s"
  [ "$(systemctl is-active $u)" = active ] || fail "$u not active"
done
grep -q '"phase": "ready"' /run/h713-hdmi-session/state.json || fail 'session state not ready'
r() { cat "$P/$1/parameters/$2" 2>/dev/null; }
for kv in h713_hdmi_receiver:clock_count:4 h713_hdmi_receiver:init_error:0 h713_hdmi_receiver:firmware_pin:Y \
          h713_hdmi_receiver:edid_ready:Y h713_hdmi_receiver:clients:2 h713_hdmi_audio:dsp_failed:N \
          h713_hdmi_audio:manage_dsp:Y h713_hdmi_audio:manage_tvfe:Y h713_hdmi_signal:ready:Y \
          h713_hdmi_signal:failed:N h713_hdmi_signal:restored:N; do
  m=${kv%%:*}; rest=${kv#*:}; k=${rest%%:*}; want=${rest#*:}
  got=$(r "$m" "$k"); echo "$m.$k=$got"
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] || fail "$m.$k is '$got', want '$want'"
done
[ -d $P/h713_ddc_pins ] || fail 'DDC pins not held'
[ -x /usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/h713-hdmi-hold-guard ] || fail 'shutdown hold guard not installed'
for d in tvfe tvcap; do
  [ "$(cat /sys/devices/h713-hdmi-$d/power/runtime_status)" = active ] || fail "$d domain inactive"
done
for m in h713_scp_probe h713_hdmi_dsp_probe h713_hdmi_power h713_edid_clock h713_hdmi_tvfe_hold; do
  [ ! -d $P/$m ] || fail "diagnostic module $m loaded"
done
dmesg | grep -E 'DSP versions|patch verified' || fail 'no DSP version log'
dmesg | grep 'DSP versions' | head -1 | grep -q '0000/0000' || fail 'DSP did not start at 0/0'
dmesg | grep -q 'patch verified versions 1/1' || fail 'DSP patch not 1/1'
grep -q H713HDMI /proc/asound/cards || fail 'no ALSA card'
cat /proc/asound/H713HDMI/pcm0c/sub0/status

ls -d /tmp/h713* /tmp/*hdmi* 2>/dev/null && echo 'note: /tmp artifacts exist (units use only /usr/lib/h713-hdmi)'
systemctl show -p ExecStart --value h713-hdmi-capture | grep -q -- '--boot-handoff' || fail 'service not using DT handoff'
echo "rtc gp6 latch unknown from Linux (U-Boot checked)"
journalctl -b -u h713-hdmi-capture -u h713-hdmi-signal --no-pager | tail -15
echo PASS

# H713 HDMI-in on the panel (HDMI panel-source design 4 and 10.26).
#
# The bridge (h713-hdmi-v4l2, node name "h713-hdmi-in") publishes its signal
# state in the "signal" attribute of its parent platform device and sends a
# "change" uevent on every transition. The device unit
# dev-h713\x2dhdmi\x2din.device is ready only while the signal is locked or
# holding; becoming ready pulls in h713-hdmi-video.service, and going
# not-ready stops it (BindsTo=). READY is set explicitly both ways because
# udev may carry properties over from the previous event (0 first, then 1
# on a match: no negative ATTRS{} match). The node's own
# name is ATTR{}, not ATTRS{}: several ATTRS{} keys must all match on ONE
# device, and "signal" lives on the parent (stage 3, 10.26.2).
SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ATTR{name}=="h713-hdmi-in", SYMLINK+="h713-hdmi-in", TAG+="systemd", ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}+="h713-hdmi-video.service"
SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ATTR{name}=="h713-hdmi-in", ENV{SYSTEMD_READY}="0"
SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ATTR{name}=="h713-hdmi-in", ATTRS{signal}=="locked*|holding*", ENV{SYSTEMD_READY}="1"

#!/bin/sh
# Install HDMI-in on the panel (HDMI panel-source design 10.26, stage 5).
# Board-only; never restarts the signal or capture owner.
#
#   sh install-hdmi-video.sh             first install (or an identical reinstall)
#   sh install-hdmi-video.sh --update    replace an installed generation, backing it
#                                        up under /var/lib/h713-hdmi-video
#   sh install-hdmi-video.sh --dry-run [--update]
#                                        every check of that mode, no writes
#   sh install-hdmi-video.sh --remove    stop, disable and remove (backups kept)
#
# Installs the bridge module and copies under /usr/lib/h713-hdmi-video, the
# two units in /etc/systemd/system and the rule in /etc/udev/rules.d, then
# enables and starts h713-hdmi-ring.service. h713-hdmi-video.service is not
# enabled: the udev rule pulls it in while the signal is locked or holding.
# H713_ROOT prefixes every path (offline tests only).
set -eu
mode=install
dry=0
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --update) mode=update ;;
        --dry-run) dry=1 ;;
        --remove) mode=remove ;;
        *) echo 'Usage: install-hdmi-video.sh [--dry-run] [--update] | --remove' >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done
[ "$mode" != remove ] || [ "$dry" = 0 ] || { echo 'install-hdmi-video: --remove has no dry run' >&2; exit 2; }
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
R=${H713_ROOT:-}
target=$R/usr/lib/h713-hdmi-video
units=$R/etc/systemd/system
rules=$R/etc/udev/rules.d
backups=$R/var/lib/h713-hdmi-video
die() { echo "install-hdmi-video: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "install-hdmi-video: $*"; }

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || [ -n "$R" ] || die 'run as root'
grep -q 'HY200 QZ713DF_A1' "$R/proc/device-tree/model" || die 'not the HY200 board'

if [ "$mode" = remove ]; then
    systemctl disable --now h713-hdmi-ring.service 2>/dev/null || true
    systemctl stop h713-hdmi-video.service 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$units/h713-hdmi-ring.service" "$units/h713-hdmi-video.service" \
        "$rules/71-h713-hdmi-in.rules"
    rm -rf "$target"
    systemctl daemon-reload
    udevadm control --reload
    lsmod | grep -q '^h713_hdmi_v4l2 ' && die 'bridge still loaded after removal'
    say "removed; console only. Backups kept in $backups"
    exit 0
fi

sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS || die 'bundle checksums'
for f in h713-hdmi-v4l2.ko 71-h713-hdmi-in.rules h713-hdmi-ring.service \
         h713-hdmi-video.service install-hdmi-video.sh; do
    grep -q "  $f\$" SHA256SUMS || die "SHA256SUMS lacks $f"
done
kernel=$(uname -r)
case "$(modinfo -F vermagic ./h713-hdmi-v4l2.ko)" in
    "$kernel "*) ;;
    *) die "module vermagic does not match the running kernel $kernel" ;;
esac
command -v gst-launch-1.0 >/dev/null || die 'gst-launch-1.0 missing'
gst-inspect-1.0 v4l2src >/dev/null || die 'v4l2src missing'
gst-inspect-1.0 kmssink >/dev/null || die 'kmssink missing'
[ -f "$units/h713-hdmi-signal.service" ] || die 'signal owner not installed'
[ -f "$units/h713-hdmi-capture.service" ] || die 'capture owner not installed'
for f in "$R/run/udev/rules.d/71-h713-hdmi-in.rules" \
         "$R/run/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-ring.service" \
         "$R/run/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-video.service"; do
    [ ! -e "$f" ] || die "runtime staging present ($f): run stage-hdmi-video.sh unstage"
done
installed=0
if [ -e "$target/SHA256SUMS" ]; then
    installed=1
    (cd "$target" && sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS) || die 'installed generation fails its checksums'
    for f in h713-hdmi-ring.service h713-hdmi-video.service; do
        cmp -s "$target/$f" "$units/$f" || die "installed $f differs from its recorded copy"
    done
    cmp -s "$target/71-h713-hdmi-in.rules" "$rules/71-h713-hdmi-in.rules" ||
        die 'installed rule differs from its recorded copy'
    if [ "$mode" != update ] && ! cmp -s SHA256SUMS "$target/SHA256SUMS"; then
        die 'a different generation is installed: use --update'
    fi
elif lsmod | grep -q '^h713_hdmi_v4l2 '; then
    die 'the bridge is loaded but not installed (a bench run?): rmmod it first'
fi

if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then
    say "dry run OK: would $([ $installed = 1 ] && echo 'replace the installed generation' || echo 'install') into $target, $units, $rules"
    exit 0
fi

if [ "$installed" = 1 ] && [ "$mode" = update ]; then
    install -d -m 0755 "$backups"
    backup=$(mktemp -d "$backups/backup.XXXXXX")
    cp -a "$target/." "$backup/"
    say "previous generation backed up to $backup"
fi
# Stop the old consumer first (the console returns), then the bridge.
for u in h713-hdmi-video.service h713-hdmi-ring.service; do
    if [ "$(systemctl show "$u" -p LoadState --value)" != not-found ]; then
        systemctl stop "$u"
    fi
done
install -d -m 0755 "$target" "$units" "$rules"
install -m 0644 h713-hdmi-v4l2.ko 71-h713-hdmi-in.rules h713-hdmi-ring.service \
    h713-hdmi-video.service SHA256SUMS "$target/"
install -m 0755 install-hdmi-video.sh "$target/"
[ ! -f stage-hdmi-video.sh ] || install -m 0755 stage-hdmi-video.sh "$target/"
install -m 0644 h713-hdmi-ring.service h713-hdmi-video.service "$units/"
install -m 0644 71-h713-hdmi-in.rules "$rules/"
systemctl daemon-reload
udevadm control --reload
systemd-analyze verify "$units/h713-hdmi-ring.service" "$units/h713-hdmi-video.service"
systemctl enable --now h713-hdmi-ring.service
sha256sum "$target/h713-hdmi-v4l2.ko" "$units/h713-hdmi-ring.service" \
    "$units/h713-hdmi-video.service" "$rules/71-h713-hdmi-in.rules"
say 'installed; the panel follows the HDMI signal. Revert: sh /usr/lib/h713-hdmi-video/install-hdmi-video.sh --remove'

# Event-driven HDMI-in on the panel, staged at runtime (HDMI panel-source
# design 10.26). Run on the board as root from the directory holding the
# bundle (h713-hdmi-v4l2.ko, 71-h713-hdmi-in.rules, h713-hdmi-ring.service,
# h713-hdmi-video.service). Everything goes under /run, so a reboot erases it;
# nothing is installed.
#
#   stage-hdmi-video.sh observe SECS   stage 1: load the bridge alone (no rule,
#                                      no units, no DRM), log every signal
#                                      transition for SECS, then unload.
#                                      No panel change.
#   ARMED=yes stage-hdmi-video.sh stage
#                                      stage 3: rule + units in /run, start the
#                                      bridge unit. The panel switches to HDMI
#                                      as soon as a signal locks.
#   stage-hdmi-video.sh status         signal, units, restarts, recent log
#   stage-hdmi-video.sh unstage        stop the units, remove the /run files
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
RUN=/run/h713-hdmi-video
ATTR=/sys/devices/platform/h713-hdmi-ring/signal

#!/bin/sh
# Board speaker route: resolve the Codec ALSA card by identity, not index.
set -eu
control=
for path in /sys/class/sound/card*/id; do
    [ "$(cat "$path")" = Codec ] || continue
    [ -z "$control" ] || { echo 'Multiple Codec cards; refusing mixer setup' >&2; exit 1; }
    card=${path%/id}; card=${card##*/card}
    control=/dev/snd/controlC$card
done
[ -n "$control" ] || { echo 'Codec ALSA card not found' >&2; exit 1; }
export CTL="$control"
ctl=/usr/lib/h713-hdmi-speaker/alsa-ctl
# Full-scale HDMI at codec gain 63 overdrives this board's speaker amplifier.
# 43 was audibly clean at 100% source volume (~23 dB below the old setting).
"$ctl" set 'DAC Playback Volume' 43
"$ctl" set 'Line Out Playback Volume' 15
"$ctl" set 'Line Out Playback Switch' 1 1
"$ctl" set 'Speaker Switch' 1

#!/bin/sh
# Board-only consumer installation; never restarts the signal or capture owner.
set -eu
update=0
case "${1-}" in
    '') ;;
    --update) update=1 ;;
    *) echo 'Usage: install-speaker.sh [--update]' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]
grep -q 'HY200 QZ713DF_A1' /proc/device-tree/model
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
command -v cc >/dev/null
pkg-config --exists gstreamer-1.0
command -v gst-launch-1.0 >/dev/null
gst-inspect-1.0 alsasrc >/dev/null
gst-inspect-1.0 alsasink >/dev/null
command -v pw-loopback >/dev/null
command -v pw-dump >/dev/null
command -v pw-cli >/dev/null
id media >/dev/null
test -S /run/user/1000/pipewire-0
[ -f /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-signal.service ]
[ -f /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-capture.service ]
target=/usr/lib/h713-hdmi-speaker
# Updates are explicit and require the old installed generation to verify.
if [ -e "$target/SHA256SUMS" ]; then
    (cd "$target"; sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)
    cmp "$target/h713-hdmi-speaker.service" /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-speaker.service
    if [ "$update" = 0 ]; then cmp SHA256SUMS "$target/SHA256SUMS"; fi
fi
stage=$(mktemp -d /tmp/h713-speaker-install.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
cc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror alsa-ctl.c -o "$stage/alsa-ctl"
cc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror hdmi-speaker.c -o "$stage/hdmi-speaker" $(pkg-config --cflags --libs gstreamer-1.0)
python3 -m py_compile pipewire-speaker.py
systemd-analyze verify "$PWD/h713-hdmi-speaker.service"
if [ -e "$target/SHA256SUMS" ] && [ "$update" = 1 ]; then
    install -d -m 0755 /var/lib/h713-hdmi-speaker
    backup=$(mktemp -d /var/lib/h713-hdmi-speaker/backup.XXXXXX)
    cp -a "$target/." "$backup/"
    echo "Speaker rollback backup: $backup"
fi
# Stop only the old speaker consumer; stopping a transient unit collects it.
if [ "$(systemctl show h713-hdmi-speaker.service -p LoadState --value)" != not-found ]; then
    systemctl stop h713-hdmi-speaker.service
fi
install -d -m 0755 "$target"
install -m 0755 "$stage/alsa-ctl" "$target/alsa-ctl"
install -m 0755 "$stage/hdmi-speaker" "$target/hdmi-speaker"
install -m 0755 enable-mixer.sh "$target/enable-mixer.sh"
install -m 0755 pipewire-speaker.py "$target/pipewire-speaker.py"
install -m 0644 alsa-ctl.c hdmi-speaker.c SHA256SUMS install-speaker.sh h713-hdmi-speaker.service "$target/"
install -m 0644 h713-hdmi-speaker.service /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-speaker.service
systemctl daemon-reload
systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-speaker.service
systemctl enable --now h713-hdmi-speaker.service
sha256sum "$target/alsa-ctl" "$target/enable-mixer.sh" /etc/systemd/system/h713-hdmi-speaker.service
echo 'Persistent speaker consumer installed; HDMI backend ownership unchanged.'

-- H713 keystone for mpv: pre-warps the picture so a tilted projector shows a
-- level rectangle (docs/keystone-plan.md). RUNS IN mpv ON THE TARGET.
--
--   mpv --script=/usr/local/share/h713/keystone.lua ...   (h713-play does this)
--
-- Every half second it reads /run/h713-keystone/state (h713-keystone's
-- daemon) and the lens geometry in /etc/h713-keystone.conf (`h713-keystone
-- lens`). While the pitch (keystone_deg) or the roll (level_deg) to correct
-- is at least min_deg, it sets keepaspect=no and blend-subtitles=video, and
-- loads keystone.glsl with the matrix below; otherwise it removes all three,
-- so a level projector costs nothing. Without a measured lens it does nothing.
-- keystone.glsl is a template: each new matrix is written into a copy under
-- /tmp and swapped in, because vo=gpu has no //!PARAM.
--
-- The model. The projector is a pinhole: panel position u (0..1, left to
-- right) and v (0..1, top to bottom) leaves the lens along the ray
-- (x, t, 1) = (s(2u - 1), tt - (tt - tb) v, 1) -- right, up, forward. The
-- projector's attitude is rebuilt from gravity: the published pitch, roll and
-- upside-down state give the up vector u in those coordinates, and the lens
-- is taken to face the wall square (its horizontal direction is the wall's
-- normal f); r = u x f. The rotation with rows r, u, f takes a ray to the
-- wall, homogeneously: (X, Y, Z) -> (X/Z, Y/Z) on a wall at unit distance.
-- The panel lands as a quadrilateral; the picture goes in the largest level
-- rectangle with the panel's aspect that fits inside it, letterboxed by the
-- video's own aspect. The shader inverts nothing: it maps each frame
-- position straight to the picture position the wall needs there.
--
-- Mirror: the display mirrors the frame (h713-mirror) after the GPU, so a
-- frame position reaches the lens as D (x, t, 1), D = diag(+-1, +-1, 1). The
-- frame's rotation is then R D -- no longer a pure rotation for the rear
-- modes, which is the point. The picture keeps whatever orientation the
-- mirror gives it uncorrected: its top goes where the frame's top points on
-- the wall, its left where the frame's left points.
--
-- Roll is levelled only in auto on a wall (the daemon's level_deg); on a
-- ceiling the picture's rotation is the projector's yaw, which gravity cannot
-- see. The OSD is drawn after every shader hook in vo=gpu and stays unwarped;
-- subtitles are blended into the video first and warp with it.
--
-- Trims (h713-keystone trim) add to what the daemon publishes: pitch, roll,
-- and yaw -- the projector turned left or right, which gravity cannot see,
-- applied as a turn of the wall about the vertical. Not under `off`. While
-- playing: Alt+Up/Down pitch, Alt+Left/Right yaw, Alt+[ / Alt+] roll, 0.5 deg
-- a press, Alt+0 resets; each is saved through h713-keystone trim --persist
-- (script-message keystone-trim AXIS +D|-D|=D|reset does the same, for a
-- remote or a test).
--
-- Corner mode (h713-keystone corners) ignores the sensor and the trims: the
-- picture fills the quadrilateral of the frame's corners moved by the
-- corner_* offsets (frame pixels, x right, y down), letterboxed inside it by
-- the video's aspect -- the square-to-quad homography, inverted. No lens
-- needed. A quadrilateral that is not convex is refused (the last good one
-- stays). While playing in corner mode Alt+1..4 select tl, tr, br, bl,
-- Alt+arrows move it corner_step px, Alt+0 resets the corners and Alt+c
-- switches to auto (and back); a marker shows the selected corner, which
-- is drawn on the OSD -- frame coordinates, after the warp -- so it sits
-- exactly on the picture's corner.
--
-- selftest=yes prints matrices for a grid of poses and quits (headless check:
-- tools/video/keystone-check.py).

local mp = require 'mp'
local msg = require 'mp.msg'

local opts = {
	state = "/run/h713-keystone/state",
	conf = "/etc/h713-keystone.conf",
	runconf = "/run/h713-keystone/conf",	-- non-persisted settings, if any
	tool = "h713-keystone",
	step = 0.5,
	corner_step = 4,		-- frame pixels per press
	shader = "/usr/local/share/h713/keystone.glsl",
	min_deg = 0.5,		-- below this the warp is off (sensor noise ~0.1 deg)
	max_deg = 40,		-- pitch; h713-keystone never asks for more than 45
	max_roll = 30,
	selftest = "",
}
require('mp.options').read_options(opts, "keystone")

local function mul(a, b)
	local r = {}
	for i = 1, 3 do
		r[i] = {}
		for j = 1, 3 do
			r[i][j] = a[i][1] * b[1][j] + a[i][2] * b[2][j] + a[i][3] * b[3][j]
		end
	end
	return r
end

local function cross(a, b)
	return {a[2] * b[3] - a[3] * b[2], a[3] * b[1] - a[1] * b[3], a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1]}
end

local function unit(a)
	local l = math.sqrt(a[1] ^ 2 + a[2] ^ 2 + a[3] ^ 2)
	return {a[1] / l, a[2] / l, a[3] / l}
end

-- Keep the part of convex polygon poly where nx x + ny y <= d.
local function clip(poly, nx, ny, d)
	local out = {}
	for i = 1, #poly do
		local p, q = poly[i], poly[i % #poly + 1]
		local fp, fq = nx * p[1] + ny * p[2] - d, nx * q[1] + ny * q[2] - d
		if fp <= 0 then out[#out + 1] = p end
		if (fp < 0 and fq > 0) or (fp > 0 and fq < 0) then
			local t = fp / (fp - fq)
			out[#out + 1] = {p[1] + t * (q[1] - p[1]), p[2] + t * (q[2] - p[2])}
		end
	end
	return out
end

-- The largest level rectangle of height/width ar inside the convex
-- quadrilateral q: its centre, width and height. For a width w, the centres
-- that fit are q's edges each moved inward by the rectangle's half extent
-- along the edge normal; bisect for the largest w that leaves any.
local function fit(q, ar)
	local area = 0
	local x0, x1, y0, y1 = math.huge, -math.huge, math.huge, -math.huge
	for i = 1, 4 do
		local p, r = q[i], q[i % 4 + 1]
		area = area + p[1] * r[2] - r[1] * p[2]
		x0, x1 = math.min(x0, p[1]), math.max(x1, p[1])
		y0, y1 = math.min(y0, p[2]), math.max(y1, p[2])
	end
	local o = area > 0 and 1 or -1		-- inside is left of each edge when CCW
	local hp = {}
	for i = 1, 4 do
		local p, r = q[i], q[i % 4 + 1]
		local nx, ny = o * (r[2] - p[2]), -o * (r[1] - p[1])
		hp[i] = {nx, ny, nx * p[1] + ny * p[2]}
	end
	local function centres(w)
		local h = w * ar
		local poly = {{x0, y0}, {x1, y0}, {x1, y1}, {x0, y1}}
		for i = 1, 4 do
			local n = hp[i]
			poly = clip(poly, n[1], n[2], n[3] - math.abs(n[1]) * w / 2 - math.abs(n[2]) * h / 2)
			if #poly == 0 then return nil end
		end
		return poly
	end
	local lo, hi = 0, x1 - x0
	for _ = 1, 60 do
		local mid = (lo + hi) / 2
		if centres(mid) then lo = mid else hi = mid end
	end
	local poly = centres(lo)
	local cx, cy = 0, 0
	for _, p in ipairs(poly) do cx, cy = cx + p[1], cy + p[2] end
	return cx / #poly, cy / #poly, lo, lo * ar
end

local function inv3(m)
	local a, b, c = m[1][1], m[1][2], m[1][3]
	local d, e, f = m[2][1], m[2][2], m[2][3]
	local g, h, i = m[3][1], m[3][2], m[3][3]
	local det = a * (e * i - f * h) - b * (d * i - f * g) + c * (d * h - e * g)
	return {{(e * i - f * h) / det, (c * h - b * i) / det, (b * f - c * e) / det},
		{(f * g - d * i) / det, (a * i - c * g) / det, (c * d - a * f) / det},
		{(d * h - e * g) / det, (b * g - a * h) / det, (a * e - b * d) / det}}
end

-- The homography taking the unit square's (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1) to the
-- quadrilateral q (Heckbert's square-to-quad).
local function square_to_quad(q)
	local x0, y0, x1, y1 = q[1][1], q[1][2], q[2][1], q[2][2]
	local x2, y2, x3, y3 = q[3][1], q[3][2], q[4][1], q[4][2]
	local dx1, dx2, dx3 = x1 - x2, x3 - x2, x0 - x1 + x2 - x3
	local dy1, dy2, dy3 = y1 - y2, y3 - y2, y0 - y1 + y2 - y3
	local g, h = 0, 0
	if math.abs(dx3) > 1e-12 or math.abs(dy3) > 1e-12 then
		local den = dx1 * dy2 - dx2 * dy1
		g = (dx3 * dy2 - dx2 * dy3) / den
		h = (dx1 * dy3 - dx3 * dy1) / den
	end
	return {{x1 - x0 + g * x1, x3 - x0 + h * x3, x0},
		{y1 - y0 + g * y1, y3 - y0 + h * y3, y0},
		{g, h, 1}}
end

-- Strictly convex, and wound one way: every turn has the same sign.
local function convex(q)
	local sign = 0
	for i = 1, 4 do
		local a, b, c = q[i], q[i % 4 + 1], q[(i + 1) % 4 + 1]
		local z = (b[1] - a[1]) * (c[2] - b[2]) - (b[2] - a[2]) * (c[1] - b[1])
		if math.abs(z) < 1e-9 then return false end
		local sz = z > 0 and 1 or -1
		if sign == 0 then sign = sz elseif sz ~= sign then return false end
	end
	return true
end

-- The letterbox: picture rectangle -> mpv's picture, stretched to the frame.
local function letterbox(va, pa)
	local lx, ly, lw, lh = 0, 0, 1, 1
	if va > pa then lh = pa / va; ly = (1 - lh) / 2 else lw = va / pa; lx = (1 - lw) / 2 end
	return {{1 / lw, 0, -lx / lw}, {0, 1 / lh, -ly / lh}, {0, 0, 1}}
end

local FW, FH = 1280, 720
local CORNERS = {"tl", "tr", "br", "bl"}
local CORNER_AT = {tl = {0, 0}, tr = {1, 0}, br = {1, 1}, bl = {0, 1}}

-- Corner mode: the quadrilateral (frame 0..1) from the settings' offsets.
local function corner_quad(cf)
	local q = {}
	for i, c in ipairs(CORNERS) do
		local at = CORNER_AT[c]
		q[i] = {at[1] + (tonumber(cf["corner_" .. c .. "_x"]) or 0) / FW,
			at[2] + (tonumber(cf["corner_" .. c .. "_y"]) or 0) / FH}
	end
	return q
end

-- Frame position -> stretched-picture position for corner mode.
local function corner_warp(q, va)
	return mul(letterbox(va, FW / FH), inv3(square_to_quad(q)))
end

-- Frame position -> stretched-picture position, homogeneous. pitch: lens tilt
-- toward the projector's own top, roll: its right side above the horizon
-- (degrees, as h713-keystone publishes them), yaw: the projector turned to
-- its right of square (degrees, a trim); inv: upside down; mode:
-- h713-mirror's number; s, tb, tt: the lens tangents (half width, bottom and
-- top edge); va: the video's aspect (width / height).
local function warp(pitch, roll, yaw, inv, mode, s, tb, tt, va)
	local p, r, y = math.rad(pitch), math.rad(roll), math.rad(yaw)
	local si = inv and -1 or 1
	-- Up, in the projector's (right, up, forward) coordinates.
	local up = {math.sin(r), si * math.cos(r) * math.cos(p), si * math.cos(r) * math.sin(p)}
	local fw = unit({-up[3] * up[1], -up[3] * up[2], 1 - up[3] * up[3]})
	local rt = cross(up, fw)
	-- Turned right by yaw: the wall's normal sits that much to its left.
	local cy, sy_ = math.cos(y), math.sin(y)
	rt, fw = {cy * rt[1] + sy_ * fw[1], cy * rt[2] + sy_ * fw[2], cy * rt[3] + sy_ * fw[3]},
		{cy * fw[1] - sy_ * rt[1], cy * fw[2] - sy_ * rt[2], cy * fw[3] - sy_ * rt[3]}
	-- The frame reaches the lens mirrored by the display: D (x, t, 1).
	local hx = mode % 2 == 1 and -1 or 1
	local vy = math.floor(mode / 2) % 2 == 1 and -1 or 1
	local R = {{rt[1] * hx, rt[2] * vy, rt[3]}, {up[1] * hx, up[2] * vy, up[3]}, {fw[1] * hx, fw[2] * vy, fw[3]}}
	-- In frame coordinates the lens tangents are mirrored too.
	local ftb, ftt = tb, tt
	if vy < 0 then ftb, ftt = -tt, -tb end
	local A = {{2 * s, 0, -s}, {0, -(ftt - ftb), ftt}, {0, 0, 1}}
	local RA = mul(R, A)
	-- The frame on the wall.
	local q = {}
	for i, c in ipairs({{0, 0}, {1, 0}, {1, 1}, {0, 1}}) do
		local X = RA[1][1] * c[1] + RA[1][2] * c[2] + RA[1][3]
		local Y = RA[2][1] * c[1] + RA[2][2] * c[2] + RA[2][3]
		local Z = RA[3][1] * c[1] + RA[3][2] * c[2] + RA[3][3]
		if Z <= 0 then return nil end
		q[i] = {X / Z, Y / Z}
	end
	local ar = (tt - tb) / (2 * s)		-- panel height / width
	local cx, cy, w, h = fit(q, ar)
	-- Wall -> the rectangle, 0..1 from the picture's top-left corner, which
	-- is wherever the frame's top-left points (sx, sy).
	local sx = (rt[1] * hx >= 0) and 1 or -1
	local sy = (up[2] * vy >= 0) and 1 or -1
	local B = {
		sx > 0 and {1 / w, 0, -(cx - w / 2) / w} or {-1 / w, 0, (cx + w / 2) / w},
		sy > 0 and {0, -1 / h, (cy + h / 2) / h} or {0, 1 / h, -(cy - h / 2) / h},
		{0, 0, 1},
	}
	-- The rectangle -> mpv's picture, stretched to the frame by keepaspect=no.
	return mul(letterbox(va, 1 / ar), mul(B, RA))
end

local function read_kv(path)
	local f = io.open(path, "r")
	if not f then return nil end
	local t = {}
	for line in f:lines() do
		local k, v = line:match("^([%w_]+)=(.*)$")
		if k then t[k] = v end
	end
	f:close()
	return t
end

local mirror_path
do
	local p = io.popen("ls /sys/bus/platform/drivers/sun50i-h713-afbd/*/mirror_mode 2>/dev/null")
	if p then mirror_path = p:read("*l"); p:close() end
end

local function mirror_mode()
	if not mirror_path then return 0 end
	local f = io.open(mirror_path, "r")
	if not f then return 0 end
	local m = tonumber(f:read("*l")) or 0
	f:close()
	return m
end

local function video_aspect()
	local vp = mp.get_property_native("video-out-params")
	if not vp or not vp.dw or not vp.dh or vp.dh <= 0 then return 16 / 9 end
	local a = vp.dw / vp.dh
	if vp.rotate and vp.rotate % 180 == 90 then a = 1 / a end
	return a
end

-- GLSL builds a mat3 column by column.
local function matrix_glsl(M)
	local c = {}
	for j = 1, 3 do
		for i = 1, 3 do c[#c + 1] = string.format("%.9g", M[i][j]) end
	end
	return "mat3(" .. table.concat(c, ", ") .. ")"
end

local template
local function shader_text(M)
	if not template then
		local f = io.open(opts.shader, "r")
		if not f then return nil end
		template = f:read("*a")
		f:close()
	end
	local text, n = template:gsub("KEYSTONE_MATRIX", matrix_glsl(M))
	return n == 1 and text or nil
end

local function matrix_opts(M)
	local o = {}
	for i = 1, 3 do
		for j = 1, 3 do
			o[#o + 1] = string.format("k%d%d=%.9g", i - 1, j - 1, M[i][j])
		end
	end
	return table.concat(o, ",")
end

local active, last = nil, nil	-- active: the generated shader in use
local serial = 0
local saved_blend

local function off(why)
	if not active then return end
	mp.commandv("change-list", "glsl-shaders", "remove", active)
	mp.set_property("keepaspect", "yes")
	if saved_blend then mp.set_property("blend-subtitles", saved_blend) end
	os.remove(active)
	active = nil
	msg.info(why)
end

-- The settings in force: the runtime file while a non-persisted change made
-- one (it then holds everything), else /etc.
local function settings()
	return read_kv(opts.runconf) or read_kv(opts.conf) or {}
end

-- The mode is a setting: read it there, not from the daemon, which only
-- republishes once the projector is still.
local function mode_of(st, cf)
	return cf.keystone or st.keystone or "auto"
end

local function install(M, what)
	local text = M and shader_text(M)
	if not text then
		msg.error(M and ("cannot use " .. opts.shader .. " (missing, or no KEYSTONE_MATRIX)")
			or "the frame does not reach the wall at this pose")
		return
	end
	serial = serial + 1
	local path = string.format("/tmp/h713-keystone-%s-%d.glsl", mp.get_property("pid"), serial)
	local f = io.open(path, "w")
	if not f then msg.error("cannot write " .. path); return end
	f:write(text)
	f:close()
	if not active then
		saved_blend = mp.get_property("blend-subtitles")
		mp.set_property("keepaspect", "no")
		mp.set_property("blend-subtitles", "video")
	end
	mp.commandv("change-list", "glsl-shaders", "append", path)
	if active then
		mp.commandv("change-list", "glsl-shaders", "remove", active)
		os.remove(active)
	end
	active = path
	msg.verbose("matrix " .. matrix_opts(M))
	msg.info(what)
end

local function apply_corners(cf, va)
	local q = corner_quad(cf)
	local key = "corners"
	for _, p in ipairs(q) do key = key .. string.format(" %.6f %.6f", p[1], p[2]) end
	key = key .. string.format(" %.4f", va)
	if key == last then return end
	last = key
	local moved = false
	for i, c in ipairs(CORNERS) do
		local at = CORNER_AT[c]
		if math.abs(q[i][1] - at[1]) > 1e-9 or math.abs(q[i][2] - at[2]) > 1e-9 then moved = true end
	end
	if not moved then off("keystone off (corners at the frame)"); return end
	if not convex(q) then
		msg.error("corners do not make a convex quadrilateral; keeping the last good one")
		mp.osd_message("keystone: those corners cross -- not applied", 2)
		return
	end
	install(corner_warp(q, va), string.format("keystone corners tl %d,%d tr %d,%d br %d,%d bl %d,%d (video aspect %.3f)",
		cf.corner_tl_x or 0, cf.corner_tl_y or 0, cf.corner_tr_x or 0, cf.corner_tr_y or 0,
		cf.corner_br_x or 0, cf.corner_br_y or 0, cf.corner_bl_x or 0, cf.corner_bl_y or 0, va))
end

local function apply()
	local st = read_kv(opts.state) or {}
	local cf = settings()
	if mode_of(st, cf) == "corners" then return apply_corners(cf, video_aspect()) end
	local k = tonumber(st.keystone_deg) or 0
	local l = tonumber(st.level_deg) or 0
	local y = 0
	if mode_of(st, cf) ~= "off" then
		k = k + (tonumber(cf.trim_pitch) or 0)
		l = l + (tonumber(cf.trim_roll) or 0)
		y = tonumber(cf.trim_yaw) or 0
	end
	-- Facing a ceiling or floor the daemon gives the tilt from its normal
	-- toward the projector's own top: an upright pose by construction.
	local inv = st.inverted == "1" and (st.surface or "wall") == "wall"
	local s, tb, tt = tonumber(cf.lens_s), tonumber(cf.lens_tb), tonumber(cf.lens_tt)
	local mode = mirror_mode()
	local va = video_aspect()
	local key = string.format("%s %s %s %s %s %s %s %d %.4f", k, l, y, inv, s, tb, tt, mode, va)
	if key == last then return end
	last = key

	if not (s and tb and tt) then
		off("keystone off: no lens geometry (h713-keystone lens)")
		return
	end
	if math.abs(k) < opts.min_deg and math.abs(l) < opts.min_deg and math.abs(y) < opts.min_deg then
		off("keystone off")
		return
	end

	k = math.max(-opts.max_deg, math.min(opts.max_deg, k))
	l = math.max(-opts.max_roll, math.min(opts.max_roll, l))
	y = math.max(-opts.max_roll, math.min(opts.max_roll, y))
	install(warp(k, l, y, inv, mode, s, tb, tt, va),
		string.format("keystone %.1f deg, level %.1f deg, yaw %.1f deg (%s, mirror %d, video aspect %.3f)",
			k, l, y, inv and "upside down" or "upright", mode, va))
end

-- Manual adjustment goes through h713-keystone (so the CLI, the remote and
-- these keys share one saved setting), then redraws at once.
local function tool(...)
	local args = {opts.tool, ...}
	args[#args + 1] = "--persist"
	local r = mp.command_native({name = "subprocess", args = args, playback_only = false,
		capture_stdout = true, capture_stderr = true})
	if not r or r.status ~= 0 then
		mp.osd_message("keystone: " .. ((r and r.stderr ~= "" and r.stderr) or "h713-keystone failed"), 3)
		return false
	end
	last = nil
	apply()
	return true
end

local selected = "tl"
local marker = mp.create_osd_overlay("ass-events")
marker.res_x, marker.res_y = FW, FH
local marker_timer

-- Corner mode: a box on the selected corner. The OSD is drawn in frame
-- coordinates after the warp, so this lands on the picture's corner itself.
local function show_corners()
	local cf = settings()
	local q = corner_quad(cf)
	local i = ({tl = 1, tr = 2, br = 3, bl = 4})[selected]
	local x = math.max(0, math.min(FW - 24, q[i][1] * FW - 12))
	local y = math.max(0, math.min(FH - 24, q[i][2] * FH - 12))
	marker.data = string.format("{\\an7\\pos(%d,%d)\\bord2\\shad0\\1c&H00FFFF&\\3c&H000000&\\p1}m 0 0 l 24 0 24 24 0 24{\\p0}", x, y)
	marker:update()
	if marker_timer then marker_timer:kill() end
	marker_timer = mp.add_timeout(3, function() marker:remove() end)
	mp.osd_message(string.format("keystone corners [%s]  tl %s,%s  tr %s,%s  br %s,%s  bl %s,%s", selected,
		cf.corner_tl_x or 0, cf.corner_tl_y or 0, cf.corner_tr_x or 0, cf.corner_tr_y or 0,
		cf.corner_br_x or 0, cf.corner_br_y or 0, cf.corner_bl_x or 0, cf.corner_bl_y or 0), 3)
end

local function show_trims()
	local cf = settings()
	mp.osd_message(string.format("keystone trim  pitch %s  yaw %s  roll %s",
		cf.trim_pitch or "0", cf.trim_yaw or "0", cf.trim_roll or "0"), 2)
end

local function in_corners()
	return mode_of(read_kv(opts.state) or {}, settings()) == "corners"
end

-- One key, two meanings: a corner move in corner mode, a trim otherwise.
local function arrow(dx, dy, trim_axis, trim_sign)
	return function()
		if in_corners() then
			local ax, d = dx ~= 0 and "x" or "y", dx ~= 0 and dx or dy
			if tool("corner", selected, ax, (d > 0 and "+" or "-") .. opts.corner_step) then show_corners() end
		elseif trim_axis then
			if tool("trim", trim_axis, (trim_sign > 0 and "+" or "-") .. opts.step) then show_trims() end
		end
	end
end

local function trim(axis, arg)		-- script-message keystone-trim
	if tool("trim", axis, arg) then show_trims() end
end

if opts.selftest ~= "" then
	-- Two lenses: this unit's (axis through the picture's centre) and one
	-- with an offset, so neither symmetry hides a sign.
	local lenses = {{0.50149, -0.28092, 0.28325}, {0.38, 0.02, 0.02 + 0.76 * 720 / 1280}}
	-- Physically sensible pairings of attitude and mirror: upright front and
	-- rear, upside-down ceiling and rear-ceiling.
	local poses = {{false, 0}, {false, 1}, {true, 3}, {true, 2}}
	for _, ln in ipairs(lenses) do
		for _, ps in ipairs(poses) do
			for _, p in ipairs({0, 10, 20, 30, -15}) do
				for _, r in ipairs({0, 5, -8}) do
					for _, y in ipairs({0, 6, -10}) do
						for _, va in ipairs({16 / 9, 2.39, 4 / 3}) do
							local M = warp(p, r, y, ps[1], ps[2], ln[1], ln[2], ln[3], va)
							print(string.format("selftest %g %g %g %d %d %.5f %.5f %.5f %.6f %s",
								p, r, y, ps[1] and 1 or 0, ps[2], ln[1], ln[2], ln[3], va, matrix_opts(M)))
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	-- Corner mode: offsets (frame px) for tl, tr, br, bl.
	local quads = {
		{{40, 30}, {-10, 60}, {-80, -20}, {0, 0}},
		{{120, 0}, {-120, 0}, {0, 0}, {0, 0}},		-- a symmetric trapezoid
		{{0, 0}, {0, 90}, {0, -90}, {0, 0}},		-- a sideways one
		{{64, 36}, {64, 36}, {64, 36}, {64, 36}},	-- a pure shift
		{{200, 150}, {-30, 10}, {-250, -40}, {15, -160}},
	}
	for _, o in ipairs(quads) do
		local cf = {}
		for i, c in ipairs(CORNERS) do
			cf["corner_" .. c .. "_x"], cf["corner_" .. c .. "_y"] = o[i][1], o[i][2]
		end
		local q = corner_quad(cf)
		for _, va in ipairs({16 / 9, 2.39, 4 / 3}) do
			local pts = {}
			for _, p in ipairs(q) do pts[#pts + 1] = string.format("%.6f %.6f", p[1], p[2]) end
			print(string.format("cornertest %s %.6f %s %s", table.concat(pts, " "), va,
				convex(q) and "convex" or "crossed", matrix_opts(corner_warp(q, va))))
		end
	end
	mp.commandv("quit")
else
	local rep = {repeatable = true}
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+UP", "keystone-up", arrow(0, -1, "pitch", 1), rep)
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+DOWN", "keystone-down", arrow(0, 1, "pitch", -1), rep)
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+RIGHT", "keystone-right", arrow(1, 0, "yaw", 1), rep)
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+LEFT", "keystone-left", arrow(-1, 0, "yaw", -1), rep)
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+]", "keystone-roll-right", arrow(0, 0, "roll", 1), rep)
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+[", "keystone-roll-left", arrow(0, 0, "roll", -1), rep)
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+0", "keystone-reset", function()
		if in_corners() then
			if tool("corner", "reset") then show_corners() end
		elseif tool("trim", "reset") then show_trims() end
	end)
	for i, c in ipairs(CORNERS) do
		mp.add_key_binding("Alt+" .. i, "keystone-select-" .. c, function()
			selected = c
			if in_corners() then show_corners() else mp.osd_message("keystone: Alt+c for corner mode", 2) end
		end)
	end
	mp.add_key_binding("Alt+c", "keystone-corner-mode", function()
		local to = in_corners() and "auto" or "corners"
		if tool(to) then
			if to == "corners" then show_corners() else mp.osd_message("keystone auto", 2) end
		end
	end)
	mp.register_script_message("keystone-trim", trim)
	mp.register_script_message("keystone-corner", function(c, ax, arg)
		if c ~= "reset" then selected = c end
		if tool("corner", c, ax, arg) then show_corners() end
	end)
	mp.register_script_message("keystone-mode", function(m) tool(m) end)
	mp.add_periodic_timer(0.5, apply)
	mp.register_event("shutdown", function() if active then os.remove(active) end end)
	mp.observe_property("video-out-params", "native", function() last = nil; apply() end)
end

# H713 HDMI-in on the panel (HDMI panel-source design 4 and 10.26).
#
# The bridge (h713-hdmi-v4l2, node name "h713-hdmi-in") publishes its signal
# state in the "signal" attribute of its parent platform device and sends a
# "change" uevent on every transition. The device unit
# dev-h713\x2dhdmi\x2din.device is ready only while the signal is locked or
# holding; becoming ready pulls in h713-hdmi-video.service, and going
# not-ready stops it (BindsTo=). READY is set explicitly both ways because
# udev may carry properties over from the previous event (0 first, then 1
# on a match: no negative ATTRS{} match). The node's own
# name is ATTR{}, not ATTRS{}: several ATTRS{} keys must all match on ONE
# device, and "signal" lives on the parent (stage 3, 10.26.2).
SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ATTR{name}=="h713-hdmi-in", SYMLINK+="h713-hdmi-in", TAG+="systemd", ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}+="h713-hdmi-video.service"
SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ATTR{name}=="h713-hdmi-in", ENV{SYSTEMD_READY}="0"
SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ATTR{name}=="h713-hdmi-in", ATTRS{signal}=="locked*|holding*", ENV{SYSTEMD_READY}="1"

/usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/h713-hd.text:
#!/bin/sh
# systemd-shutdown hook (runs last, root read-only, journald gone). If any HDMI
# owner module is still loaded, teardown failed somewhere and holds were
# retained (MIPS unparked, SCP payload possibly still asserting HPD). Those
# need a physical cold cycle, which a warm reset cannot give, so a reboot or
# kexec is turned into a poweroff, lamp off first. Poweroff/halt proceed as
# requested. Never touches hardware itself.
M=${H713_GUARD_SYSMODULE:-/sys/module}
OFF=${H713_GUARD_LAMP_OFF:-/usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/h713-off}
POWEROFF=${H713_GUARD_POWEROFF:-systemctl --force --force poweroff}
held=
for m in h713_hdmi_signal h713_ddc_pins h713_scp_probe h713_hdmi_audio h713_hdmi_receiver; do
  [ ! -d "$M/$m" ] || held="$held $m"
done
[ -n "$held" ] || exit 0
case "$1" in
reboot|kexec)
  msg="h713-hdmi-hold-guard: $1 refused, HDMI holds retained ($held ); powering off, cold cycle required"
  echo "$msg" > /dev/kmsg 2>/dev/null; echo "$msg" > /dev/console 2>/dev/null
  "$OFF" poweroff
  exec $POWEROFF;;
*)
  msg="h713-hdmi-hold-guard: $1 with HDMI holds retained ($held ); cold cycle required"
  echo "$msg" > /dev/kmsg 2>/dev/null; echo "$msg" > /dev/console 2>/dev/null;;
esac
exit 0
